_doc: Adapter-specific overlay on Next.js's own test/deploy-tests-manifest.json, merged by
Version-2 semantics: `suites.<file>.failed[]` holds FULL test names, which the runner turns
into a negated --testNamePattern; `rules.exclude[]` drops whole files before they are built.
Both merge additively with upstream's entries, and an exact-filename exclude wins over an
inclusion. Unknown keys (like this one) are ignored by the parser.
ONLY record a failure here once its cause is understood and is NOT the adapter's. Anything
listed stops being visible, so an entry added on a hunch hides a real bug — which is exactly
why cache-components-allow-otel-spans is deliberately absent below.

_reason: The adapter is MORE correct than the deploy target this expectation was written for.
Upstream's own comment marks the Vercel behaviour as the deviation, and the test asserts
it. The adapter does a blocking revalidation when the entry has expired, which is what
`expire` means; asserting otherwise would mean regressing to match a known-wrong target.
Deploy and build both succeed here — only the assertion diverges — so this is a
case-level exclusion rather than a file exclusion.
failed: expire-time should do a blocking revalidation when the cache entry has expired

test/e2e/app-dir/next-dist-client-esm-im: Upstream Turbopack panic, not an adapter failure: the BUILD aborts with
`FATAL: An unexpected Turbopack error occurred` and writes a Rust panic log, failing to

parse ordinary JSX (`return

hello world

;`) in the fixture. Excluded at FILE level
rather than case level because the deploy never completes — a case exclusion would still
pay for the build and still emit a panic log every run.

test/e2e/app-dir/cache-components-allow-: `should allow creating Spans from a tracer acquired before provider registration` —
INVESTIGATED 2026-07-26 and CONFIRMED AN ADAPTER BUG. Do not record it here; it must stay
visible until fixed.
Evidence (same build, served two ways, /novel/early-span):
next start          -> 200, 7658 bytes, contains `class="result"` and `>42<`
adapter pool server -> 200, 1358 bytes, neither, in 21ms
The pool server's shell ends `<!--$--><!--/$-->`: an EMPTY, already-closed Suspense
boundary — no fallback, no content — where upstream renders the resolved content. 21ms vs
the ~1000ms the sibling pages take is the same story: the dynamic half never ran.
Not an instrumentation-ordering problem, which was the first hypothesis: the log shows
`instrumentation register() completed` before serving and the page returns 200, so the
component's `if (!tracer) throw` never fired — the tracer was there.
Narrow: /novel/server and /novel/fallback have dynamic holes on the same route pattern and
both resume correctly (11940 and 2422 bytes, results present). The one thing early-span
does differently is wrap its returned JSX in an OTEL `context.with(ctx, async () => ...)`,
so the suspect is the resume path losing that async context.
Predates the security work (it is in the previous phase's failure notes verbatim).
LOCALIZED 2026-07-26 to one line: the minimalMode gate in pool-server/dispatch.ts. It goes
non-minimal only for `(entrypointOwnsPprShell || incrementalCacheShared) && (handlerPprInfo
|| handlerPprRootParams)`, and this route has neither a build shell nor root params, so it
stays MINIMAL — which is the case the gate's own comment describes: minimal mode answers a
document with the bare postponed shell plus `x-nextjs-postponed: 1` and expects the PLATFORM
to run the resume dance, which this adapter does not implement for an entry-owned shell.
MEASURED, do not repeat: adding `|| handlerPprCapable` to that gate DOES fix early-span, but
it is not the fix. It breaks a sibling in the same file (`prerendering at runtime - inside a
Cache Components`) and re-breaks app-dir/fallback-shells with 5 failures — `without IO should
start and not postpone the response` plus four `page not wrapped in Suspense` cases. That is
the same regression the gate was narrowed to avoid.
What a real fix needs: a discriminator between a shell-less PPR route whose dynamic hole IS
behind a Suspense boundary (early-span — upstream prerenders then resumes it in one blocking
navigation) and one that has no Suspense boundary above the params access (fallback-shells'
without-suspense/without-io — upstream renders those fully dynamically and never postpones).
rootParams does not separate them; both are empty. Either derive that from the build output,
or implement the resume dance for an entry-owned shell so minimal mode stops being a
truncation. Designed work, not a patch.
Reproduce: run this single test with NEXT_TEST_SKIP_CLEANUP=1 and a no-op
NEXT_TEST_CLEANUP_SCRIPT_PATH, then curl /novel/early-span on the preserved pool server
and diff it against `next start` on the same .next directory.
